Hedge fund honcho Sam Leffell has views. I got to know Sam while researching [ChatGPT's predictive abilities](https://www.businessinsider.com/chatgpt-economists-secret-prediction-game-openai-2025-12). He uses that leading AI tool constantly for work and in his personal life.

He also tried Google's [Gemini](https://www.businessinsider.com/sundar-pichai-cheeseburger-google-comeback-2025-11) earlier this year and became obsessed with a [Gmail](https://www.businessinsider.com/google-gmail-of-the-future-looks-incredible-integrated-ai-assistant-2024-5) feature called Polish that uses AI to improve any email with at least 12 words in it. You just press Alt+H on Windows PCs, or Option+H on Macs, and Gemini swoops into action. (That's polish, the shining process, not Polish the language).

Sam said this was the most useful Gemini feature. "Writing emails now takes a fraction of the time it used to," he said. "I still make picky edits, but it's a lot quicker and better."

ADVERTISEMENT

Here's the wrinkle: He turned off his Gemini paid subscription after a while because, anecdotally for him, it was not as good as ChatGPT. Then, the Polish feature from his Gmail suddenly disappeared. Unacceptable!

"That surprised me," Sam said. "So now I'm paying Google a certain amount each month, just to have this button to polish all my emails. That's how valuable this is."

The first paid tier of Gemini is $20 a month. That's a lot for one feature.

# Google's Year-End Wrap-Up Video Gets Ripped Over 'Embarrassing' Omissions

Critics said the company missed the mark with its annual "Year in Search" video.

By [Ben Blanchet](https://www.huffpost.com/author/ben-blanchet)

LOADINGERROR LOADING

[Google](https://www.huffpost.com/news/topic/google) dropped its “Year in Search” video for 2025 on Monday and some internet users aren’t liking the results. **(You can watch it [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vv_sjpclsZ8).)**

The year-end wrap-up video, which [Google](https://www.huffpost.com/impact/topic/google) has [released annually](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLYKIFv1fATsHOEDaOeYeTj_cSJqJ84ITm) since 2010, has typically featured clips of trends and major events, such as 2020 [Black Lives Matter protests](https://youtu.be/rokGy0huYEA?si=iXqmY5bkKsZ953ba&t=89), the [removal of the Confederate battle flag](https://youtu.be/q7o7R5BgWDY?si=L9loLdfYmrvRszXx&t=21) flying outside the South Carolina state Capitol and families [reuniting at the U.S.-Mexico border](https://youtu.be/KIViy7L_lo8?si=g0tc5Sq6urheNkHi&t=105). The annual video has also looped in clips of [someone coming out as transgender](https://youtu.be/q7o7R5BgWDY?si=Jd6__eMqU0t6RwhG&t=90) and footage from [the 2017 Women’s March](https://youtu.be/vI4LHl4yFuo?si=kjy79wR0A7bjV4me&t=110) on the day after [Donald Trump](https://www.huffpost.com/news/topic/donald-trump)’s first inauguration.

Advertisement

Google billed this year’s recap video as showcasing ways people “reimagined their worlds” and featured its typical assortment of pop culture clips — ranging from Lady Gaga and Lububus — before flipping to praise artificial intelligence.

The 2025 video also included footage from the Southern California wildfires, Trump [shaking hands with first responders](https://youtu.be/Vv_sjpclsZ8?si=doUcrWhga982sKpU&t=142) while touring the damage from the Central Texas floods and Erika Kirk [declaring that she was choosing “courage” and “family”](https://youtu.be/Vv_sjpclsZ8?si=WcR1G5Owkg-Noj3a&t=150) during the memorial service for her late husband, controversial podcaster Charlie Kirk.

Advertisement

On Monday, a number of YouTubers shared comments claiming this year’s video missed the mark and pointed out the lack of clips on wars in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan. It also failed to cover Trump’s immigration crackdown as well as the massive No Kings protests against the president.

“Charlie Kirk in there but nothing about Gaza bro are we fr 😭😭,” [one user wrote](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vv_sjpclsZ8&lc=UgzkgiB8--7EjIlbtit4AaABAg).

YouTuber @megbishop\_ ripped Google’s “embarrassing” approach, as well, and accused the company of skipping “a ton of top searches” to avoid controversy.

HuffPost has reached out to Google for comment.

Others on X, Bluesky and Threads also slammed the video.

“That ’2025 — Year in Search’ video by Google is pure AmeriKKKan propaganda. I wasted my time and data, and I want it back,” [wrote @shingiv on X](https://x.com/shingiv/status/1998094017993777259?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E1998094017993777259%7Ctwgr%5E9fa7e35c93ea0ae028e5a1ab783b7aaed933f820%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fathena.huffpost.net%2Fus%2Fcms).

Advertisement

“This amazing short feature from Google is what life would be like if you simply accepted the shit show that is the world today and diverted all of your attention to the propaganda of one of the world’s most devious, harmful, and evil corporations,” [wrote another user on Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/swedetrap.bsky.social/post/3m7ifflj66k2y).

You can check out those reactions and more below.

# Google’s Year in Search Captures 2025's Curveballs, From Labubus to KPop Demon Hunters

## The campaign also showcases big surprises like the Luka Dončić trade

By [Samantha Nelson](https://www.adweek.com/contributor/samantha-nelson/)

[Google](https://www.adweek.com/media/google-gemini-ads-2026/) is celebrating the biggest surprises of 2025 and the ways people are rethinking what is possible with its 15th annual Year in Search campaign.

The work continues last year’s theme by highlighting breakout searches that rose more than 5,000% in 2025 compared with 2024.

The nearly four minute film, created by Google Brand Studio, moves through a wide range of moments from sports, pop culture, politics, and religion that caught the world off guard.

These include Luka Dončić being traded to the Los Angeles Lakers, Pope Francis becoming the first American pope, Zohran Mamdani winning the New York mayoral race, and the success of Netflix’s hit KPop Demon Hunters.

The campaign also shows the ways people turned to Google for answers about trends such as Labubus and the meaning of 6-7. It includes somber moments, as well, reflecting on the assassination of Charlie Kirk and the response to severe floods in Texas and wildfires in Los Angeles.

Google released the ad on social media along with a Google Doodle inspired by the breakout searches and a set of videos that explore moments from the main film, such as India’s Women’s Cricket World Cup and Lady Gaga’s tour The Mayhem Ball.

[Google Tells Advertisers It’ll Bring Ads to Gemini in 2026](https://www.adweek.com/media/google-gemini-ads-2026/)

[According to Google](https://blog.google/products/search/year-in-search-2025/), people asked questions in more conversational ways this year. The tech giant saw more queries starting as, “What’s the deal with…?” (Example: “What’s the deal with 6-7?”)

Searches for “Tell me about…” were up 70% year over year, and queries starting with “How do I…” increased 25% from last year. The latter group included questions like, “How do I know if my Labubu is real?”

# Google executive sees AI search as expansion for web

By [Jeffrey Dastin](/authors/jeffrey-dastin/) and [Krystal Hu](/authors/krystal-hu/)

* Summary
* Companies

* Google sees AI search as growth chance, not threat to web
* Google says new ads format will evovle in AI search
* Google to add more AI features into search

Dec 4 (Reuters) - A Google search executive on Thursday pushed back against fears that its AI-powered search will harm web publishers and its advertising business, calling the technology an “expansionary moment” for the internet.

Speaking at the Reuters NEXT conference in New York, Robby Stein, vice president of product for Google Search, addressed concerns that the company’s efforts to provide more AI-powered features — which deliver direct answers to queries — would reduce traffic to external websites.

Sign up[here.](undefined?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fbusiness%2Fmedia-telecom%2Fgoogle-executive-sees-ai-search-expansion-web-2025-12-04%2F)

“Google sends billions and billions and billions of clicks out every single day, and the outbound clicks are largely stable. So that’s actually not changing,” Stein said, adding that new ways people are searching, such as using their phone cameras or asking long, complex questions, are creating new opportunities. “We think over time that’s expansionary. The pie is growing very, very fast.”

AI TRANSITION LIKENED TO MOBILE MIGRATION

Stein also sought to allay investor concerns that a shift to conversational AI could disrupt Google’s lucrative advertising model. He compared the current transition to the migration from desktop to mobile, saying advertising will evolve to fit the new format.

Ads in an AI chat experience can be “incredibly helpful,” he said, citing an example of a user with a raccoon problem being offered relevant products.

Stein’s comments came as reports emerged that rival OpenAI had declared a “code red” to improve ChatGPT amid growing competition from Google. The tech giant Alphabet [(GOOGL.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/GOOGL.O) has appeared to wave off early threats to its core business with more diverse experiences, frontier model launches and viral products such as its photo-generation tool Nano Banana. Shares of Google have risen nearly 67% this year, fueled by [growth in its cloud unit](/business/ai-turned-google-cloud-also-ran-into-alphabets-growth-driver-2025-10-31/).

Stein's remarks counter a growing narrative from media organizations that AI will decimate their traffic and revenue, while also reassuring Wall Street that Google’s core cash-generating machine is not at risk as it revamps its flagship product.

“Google cares about the web more than anyone,” Stein said, describing AI as a “powerful discovery engine” that will help users go deeper by linking out to sources.

When asked whether Google felt “unshackled” to innovate following a [U.S. antitrust ruling](/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/google-keeps-chrome-apple-deal-must-share-data-big-antitrust-ruling-2025-09-02/) that allows Google to keep its Chrome browser, Stein downplayed the case’s impact. “The model’s capability is the thing that’s driving the innovation and the excitement,” he said.

Google’s push into generative AI for its search engine, which followed a clumsy start in 2023, has met with alarm from the publishing industry. Several media leaders have warned of a [sharp decline](/legal/litigation/googles-ai-overviews-hit-by-eu-antitrust-complaint-independent-publishers-2025-07-04/) in referral traffic, a fear backed by a Pew Research study this year that found AI summaries made people less likely to click on source links.

How much would you pay for a single AI killer app?

Hedge fund honcho Sam Leffell has views. I got to know Sam while researching [ChatGPT's predictive abilities](https://www.businessinsider.com/chatgpt-economists-secret-prediction-game-openai-2025-12). He uses that leading AI tool constantly for work and in his personal life.

He also tried Google's [Gemini](https://www.businessinsider.com/sundar-pichai-cheeseburger-google-comeback-2025-11) earlier this year and became obsessed with a [Gmail](https://www.businessinsider.com/google-gmail-of-the-future-looks-incredible-integrated-ai-assistant-2024-5) feature called Polish that uses AI to improve any email with at least 12 words in it. You just press Alt+H on Windows PCs, or Option+H on Macs, and Gemini swoops into action. (That's polish, the shining process, not Polish the language).

Sam said this was the most useful Gemini feature. "Writing emails now takes a fraction of the time it used to," he said. "I still make picky edits, but it's a lot quicker and better."

Here's the wrinkle: He turned off his Gemini paid subscription after a while because, anecdotally for him, it was not as good as ChatGPT. Then, the Polish feature from his Gmail suddenly disappeared. Unacceptable!

"That surprised me," Sam said. "So now I'm paying Google a certain amount each month, just to have this button to polish all my emails. That's how valuable this is."

The first paid tier of Gemini is $20 a month. That's a lot for one feature.

## The EU has concerns Google might be distorting competition by giving itself privileged access to publisher’s content

By

[Edith Hancock](https://www.wsj.com/news/author/edith-hancock)

Updated 
 ET

---

The European Union opened an antitrust investigation into Google related to its artificial-intelligence practices. dado ruvic/Reuters

The European Union opened an antitrust investigation into [Alphabet’s](/market-data/quotes/GOOGL) [GOOGL -2.29%decrease; red down pointing triangle](/market-data/quotes/GOOGL) Google, citing concerns about how it uses uploaded content on platforms such as YouTube to power and train its artificial-intelligence tools.

The European Commission said Tuesday that it is looking into whether Google is distorting competition by imposing unfair terms and conditions on publishers or by giving itself privileged access to their content. The EU’s executive arm said such practices could put Google’s own AI tools at an advantage over competitors.

I know this page is a joke, but in the interest of accuracy, a terminological comment: we don't call it a "hallucination" if a model complies exactly with what a prompt asked for and produces a prediction, exactly as requested. Rater, "hallucinations" are spurious replacements of factual knowledge with fictional material caused by the use of statistical process (the pseudo random number generator used with the "temperature" parameter of neural transformers): token prediction without meaning representation.  [typo fixed] | | | |  | | --- | | [articlepan](user?id=articlepan) [50 minutes ago](item?id=46217166)  | [parent](#46216933) | [next](#46217410) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   I agree with your first paragraph, but not your second. Models can still hallucinate when temperature is set to zero (aka when we always choose the highest probability token from the model's output token distribution). In my mind, hallucination is when some aspect of the model's response should be consistent with reality but is not, and the reality-inconsistent information is not directly attributable or deducible from (mis)information in the pre-training corpus.  While hallucination can be triggered by setting the temperature high, it can also be the result of many possible deficiencies in model pre- and post- training that result in the model outputting bad token probability distributions. Asking the model to create a work of fiction and it complying isn't a pathology. Mozart wasn't "hallucinating" when he created "The Marriage of Figaro".  [reply](reply?id=46217061&goto=item%3Fid%3D46205632%2346217061) | | | |  | | --- | | [Olreich](user?id=Olreich) [46 minutes ago](item?id=46217195)  | [root](#46216933) | [parent](#46217061) | [next](#46217499) [[–]](javascript:void(0))   But many artists are hallucinating when they envisioned some of their pieces. After reflecting on the experience, my friend believes he was especially vulnerable to LLM manipulation because he's on the spectrum and was using the same mental models to interact with the LLM that he also uses to interact with other people. # Exclusive: Meta strikes multiple AI deals with news publishers

* [Sara Fischer](https://www.axios.com/authors/sara)

[Add Axios on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=axios.com)

Add Axios as your preferred source to

see more of our stories on Google.

[Add Axios on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=axios.com)

[Meta](https://www.axios.com/2025/10/16/meta-poaches-apple-ai-engineer-executive) on Friday said it has struck several commercial AI data agreements with news publishers ranging from USA Today, People Inc., CNN, Fox News, The Daily Caller, Washington Examiner and Le Monde.

**Why it matters:** Meta backed away from compensating news companies several years ago, but has resumed paying for editorial content as it invests more in its AI chat tools that require real-time access to verified news.



**Zoom in:** The [new agreements](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/12/bringing-more-real-time-news-and-content-to-meta-ai/) allow Meta to access content from its partners to provide real-time answers to user queries about news and current events in its [Meta AI chatbot](https://www.axios.com/2023/09/27/meta-debuts-new-artificial-intelligence-chatbot).

* Like its previously announced [deal](https://www.axios.com/2024/10/25/meta-reuters-ai-news-facebook-instagram) with Reuters, the new agreements are multiyear deals where publishers are compensated for the use of their content.
* The new deals are meant to provide users with a broader range of verified content that spans global news, entertainment and lifestyle.
* Over time, the company plans to add more news partners and topics while expanding new features for users looking to access to real-time information.

**How it works:** Meta's AI chatbot is integrated into the search and messaging features on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger.

* When users ask Meta's AI chatbot a question that requires a real-time news response, they will not only receive information about the source that Meta AI has pulled the answers from, but the chatbot will also link out to articles on the publishers' websites.

**Zoom out:** It's notable that Meta is partnering with conservative news organizations, such as Fox News, The Daily Caller and Washington Examiner, because of its complicated history with making news partnership decisions.

* In 2016, Facebook was [accused](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2016/may/10/facebook-denies-censoring-conservative-trending-news) of censoring conservative stories in its trending topics feature. That allegation, which it denied, kicked off years of scrutiny from Republicans that the tech giant was biased against conservative voices.
* When the company launched its News Tab in 2019, it [included](https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/26/media/facebook-news-breitbart) conservative outlets, such as Breitbart, as sources.

**The big picture:** While users can still share news across Meta's non-AI products, its platforms — specifically Facebook — are no longer built to be hubs for sharing news articles. Rather, they have [shifted](https://www.axios.com/2022/07/21/facebook-tiktok-feed-changes) to elevate viral video content.

* Facebook killed its [News Tab](https://about.fb.com/news/2024/02/update-on-facebook-news-us-australia/) in the U.S. in 2024 and [ended](https://www.axios.com/2022/07/28/meta-publishers-news-funding-cut) its lucrative news publisher payout program in 2022.

# 谷歌（近期新闻）综合总结报告

## 1) 总体概述
近期关于谷歌的新闻以“人工智能驱动的产品变革”和“围绕AI训练数据与内容使用的监管/舆论风险”为主线。同时，谷歌也面临来自公众舆论（品牌/文化类回顾视频被批评）、开发者/社区对模型输出可靠性的讨论，以及竞争对手与出版方在内容与AI合作方面的新布局。公司一方面积极把AI能力嵌入搜索与生产力产品（如Gmail 的“Polish”等），并对广告与流量影响做出业务层面的安抚；另一方面则须应对欧盟监管调查、舆论批评以及模型“幻觉”/可信度争议。

---

## 2) 重点事件（2–3 个）
1. AI 驱动的“新型搜索”定位与业务宣示（Reuters）
   - 谷歌搜索副总裁 Robby Stein 在路透NEXT 上表态：AI 搜索是对互联网的“扩张时刻”，不会削弱外部网站流量，出站点击稳定，并认为广告会像移动时代一样向对话式/AI 格式演进。
   - 目的：安抚媒体与投资者对流量与广告收入被侵蚀的担忧，强调产品创新与长期生态扩张。

2. 欧盟对谷歌使用在线内容训练AI的调查（The Wall Street Journal）
   - 欧盟监管机构对谷歌是否在未经许可/补偿的情况下使用在线内容来训练其AI模型开展调查，属于对AI训练数据合规性的直接监管压力。
   - 影响：可能带来法律、合规成本上升，并影响谷歌与内容提供者（新闻媒体、出版商等）的关系与商业模式。

3. 品牌/公关与可信性挑战：年终回顾视频被批评 + 模型“幻觉”讨论（HuffPost、Hacker News）
   - 谷歌2025年“Year in Search”视频因偏重流行文化和对AI的赞誉、忽略重大社会议题遭网友抨击，反映公众对公司价值观与叙事的敏感性。
   - 开发者/社区层面，Gemini Pro 3 在 Hacker News 的演示引发关于“hallucination”定义与模型输出可信度的讨论，凸显技术信任问题。

---

## 3) 趋势分析（含对各方影响）
1. AI 正在被系统性嵌入产品矩阵，走向“体验层”而非仅是研究/后端能力
   - 证据：Gmail 的“Polish”、搜索界面对话式查询、Gemini 在社区演示等都显示 Google 把模型能力直接放到用户工作流中。
   - 影响：短期提升用户黏性与工作效率，长期将催化新的付费/变现模式（单一“杀手级”AI应用的付费意愿讨论表明用户愿为显著效益付费）。

2. 广告与流量商业模式面临重塑，但公司试图降低市场担忧
   - 谷歌强调出站点击量稳固，认为广告将适配对话式AI格式（类似移动化转变）。
   - 观察点：若AI结果替代部分页面访问，广告位与计量方式需调整；广告商与谷歌需重新定义曝光与转化的计价方式。

3. 监管与内容权利争议上升，风险由合规转为可能的商业重构
   - 欧盟调查显示监管对AI训练数据来源更严；同时媒体与平台间的商业关系（如 Meta 与出版商达成多项AI协议）正在重塑内容供应链。
   - 影响：谷歌可能需要与出版商重新谈判数据使用与补偿机制，或面对罚款/限制，对成本和模型训练策略有直接影响。

4. 公众信任与模型可靠性成为非技术性风险
   - 年终视频的舆论风波与Gemini“幻觉”争议说明：公司不仅要推进功能，更需管理价值观叙事与输出准确性/可解释性。
   - 影响：品牌声誉波动会影响用户、监管与企业客户的接受度；技术团队需把“可用且可信”作为产品优先项。

5. 竞争与生态动态：出版商与平台达成独立协议，行业生态在重构
   - Meta 与新闻出版商的多项AI协议提示内容提供者在与大型平台谈判新的价值分配；谷歌在此环境下既是竞争者
